subject.title: RFC: TapesClaw for Claw telemetry storage and querying

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a first-party, default-enabled durable telemetry store and new evidence hook, or require telemetry to start as an optional external plugin using only a narrowly approved generic seam?
rationale: This choice sets long-lived product, privacy, storage, and plugin-contract policy that cannot be resolved mechanically from the RFC text.

options.title: Adopt an external-plugin-first direction
options.body: Keep Tapes optional and approve only a generic, bounded capture/evidence contract after the RFC specifies its privacy and lifecycle constraints.

options.title: Sponsor a bundled telemetry direction
options.body: Accept a first-party bundled design only after the RFC defines consent, retention, storage ownership, redaction, failure behavior, and the supported plugin API.

options.title: Defer the proposal
options.body: Leave the RFC draft until an owner confirms that durable telemetry is a current roadmap priority.

recommendation.title: Adopt an external-plugin-first direction
recommendation.body: Keep Tapes optional and approve only a generic, bounded capture/evidence contract after the RFC specifies its privacy and lifecycle constraints.

likelyOwner.reason: The RFC identifies Patrick-Erichsen as the participant in the motivating design discussion, making him the best available routing candidate from the supplied context.
